videos.title: Orchestrate your Agents with Microsoft Agent Framework
videos.focus: Reviewing a graph-based multi-agent workflow with checkpoints and human review
videos.summary: Microsoft's Azure Friday episode walks through a graph-based Agent Framework workflow that coordinates specialized agents, synthesizes a PowerPoint and exposes intermediate progress. The official page documents chapters, streaming, checkpointing and human-in-the-loop support. It is a developer-oriented product demonstration, so teams should independently test reliability, permissions and recovery before adopting the pattern.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the chaptered demonstration to sketch one multi-step workflow, assign each agent a bounded role, expose checkpoints to reviewers and test failure recovery before connecting the orchestration to consequential data or actions.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the official episode description and complete chapter sequence, then verified the exact 721.1667-second Microsoft Learn player.

playback_evidence.method: Fresh signed-out Chrome session loaded the official Microsoft Learn episode and activated its HTML5 player.
playback_evidence.result: Observed the duration-matched 12:01 player with readyState 4, paused false and currentTime advancing beyond five seconds.

quality_review.learning_objective: Map a multi-step task into bounded agent roles, observable graph transitions, checkpoints and a human review point before final output.
quality_review.practical_action: Draw one workflow as a short graph, label each agent's input and output, add a checkpoint before the consequential step and test an interrupted run.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected during same-edition recovery because its exact official player advanced signed out, its chaptered lesson is independently reviewable and the failed Vidyard player did not pass the protected gate.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the full official description and chapters covering introduction, workflow visualization, source PowerPoint, agent demo, repository and closing guidance.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: Microsoft demonstrates its own framework, so the orchestration and review pattern is retained while product capability and reliability claims remain first-party.
transferable_takeaways: Assign each agent one bounded role with an explicit input and reviewable output.
Expose graph transitions and checkpoints so reviewers can inspect progress before final synthesis.
Test interrupted execution and human escalation before the workflow touches consequential systems.

videos.title: From a Workday Expert: Self-Service Agent
videos.focus: Configuring and testing a noncoding employee self-service agent
videos.summary: Workday Education demonstrates registering a Self-Service Agent, enabling Skills and tools, configuring fallback guidance, checking domain security and testing access before deployment. The lesson also shows employee and manager use cases. It reflects Workday’s product and automation claims, so teams should validate outcomes and permissions in a nonproduction environment.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the procedure to create a configuration checklist: confirm required security policies, register the agent, enable only needed capabilities, define fallback behavior and test each user group before release.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete 1,361-line English caption transcript, dated Workday lesson page and exact 1,005.888-second player.

playback_evidence.method: Fresh signed-out Chrome session loaded the official Workday lesson and activated the visible HTML5 play control.
playback_evidence.result: Observed duration 1,005.888 seconds with readyState 4, paused false and currentTime advancing beyond 6.10 seconds.

quality_review.learning_objective: Configure a self-service agent through registration, limited capabilities, fallback handling, security verification and user-specific testing before production release.
quality_review.practical_action: Create a five-step checklist covering registration, capability scope, fallback, domain security and test evidence for each intended user group.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected as the justified up-to-twenty-minute fallback because it teaches a complete administrative procedure, uses a distinct original publisher and passed duration-matched signed-out playback.

transferable_takeaways: Verify domain security before enabling capabilities for any employee or manager group.
Define fallback guidance so unsupported requests reach an accountable human channel.
Test normal, missing-access and prohibited-action cases in a nonproduction environment before release.
